newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures mostly lower in switch trades.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures mostly lower in switch trades.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee erased early gains to end Tuesday midsession mostly down in spread-related activity as spot May neared the first tender day on Thursday.
By the morning recess, May led losers and fell $13 at $1,532. But second-position July held at the key support at $1,600, unchanged from Monday's finish.
May/July switches provided the bulk of the business as operators liquidated their May positions and moved further out.
Traders said May/July switches were traded at $65 this morning against $59 on Monday afternoon.
The widening of the May discount to July reflected mounting worries over the new LIFFE grading terms which come into effect with the July contract.
"I think the concerns there are purely on the technical issue on grading the coffee and re-grading the coffee. If you take up May you are not sure you can re-tender it in July," said a trader.
"That's what driven the switch to a big discount, bigger than it should really," he said.
"But I think it won't go much below this. If it comes much below this some body will have the confidence to buy it," the trader added.
By the close on Monday, May's uncovered positions fell by a large 1,959 lots to 5,692 but July and September each registered a rise.
Overall volume stood at 3,913 lots by Tuesday midsession.

The volume of coffee being put up for grading continued to rise. By late Monday, a further 65 lots were graded, bringing the total to 2,496 of which 1,565 were untenderables. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
